Then a webhook aimed at cloud metadata, and a forged webhook signature.

layers.title: FHIR servers
layers.intro: Healthcare phase 1's group I, declared in ADR-105 before the FHIR connector's code existed (HC-P02 built it). A FHIR server answers success in ways that don't mean what the agent says: a conditional create that matched an existing resource, an update the server kept as the old version, a field the server changed, a 5xx after it committed, a stale If-Match, a type outside the connector's list, and PHI that must never reach a stored record. The cases run against an in-process FHIR R4 server that answers the way HAPI FHIR JPA did in HC-P05's spike. A version another writer or a forged request id made, a transaction that committed more than it reported and HAPI's large-object rows are Proven (L2) cases that wait on HC-P05; the delete rule waits on the healthcare-fhir pack (HC-P06).

cases.title: A conditional create (If-None-Exist) is answered 200 with an existing resource while the agent reports it created one

cases.actual: MISMATCH at L1 (fhir_conditional_matched: the server returned an existing resource version and this action created none; never VERIFIED)

cases.title: An update with no change: the server keeps the version and answers 200

cases.actual: VERIFIED at L1 (the fields match) with the note fhir_no_new_version naming the unchanged version; the record never shows a new version

cases.title: The server stores a different value in a field the agent set and answers success
cases.expected: MISMATCH at L1 (fhir_field_changed with the field's path; server-added meta and generated narrative don't count)
cases.actual: MISMATCH at L1 (fhir_field_changed with the field's path; server-added meta and generated narrative don't count)

cases.actual: UNVERIFIABLE (the action is unknown; fhir_history_no_match names the gap); never VERIFIED and never MISMATCH

layers.title: Hostile MCP servers and upstreams
layers.intro: S34's group Q. The upstream is the attacker: tool descriptions that carry instructions, a tool that changes after it was listed, two servers with the same tool name, huge or deeply nested results, a server that is down or hangs, a server that asks the client's model for text, a live Stripe key, and a webhook host that turns into cloud metadata.

layers.title: Resources, records and output
layers.intro: S34's group R. Inputs built to exhaust or mislead: policy and CEL bombs, a forked deed chain, a signed intent from the wrong time, injection through the optional AI wording of suggestions, oversized and deeply nested JSON, and control characters aimed at terminals and logs.

cases.expected: REJECTED (policy_invalid: yaml_alias and yaml_too_complex; request_too_large for 10^6 nodes and the 20 MiB file) in < 200 ms; server memory grows < 64 MiB
cases.actual: REJECTED (policy_invalid: yaml_alias and yaml_too_complex; request_too_large for 10^6 nodes and the 20 MiB file) in < 200 ms; server memory grows < 64 MiB

cases.expected: REJECTED (policy_invalid: cel_nesting and cel_cost at lint); at run time the rule stops at its limit and the action is denied, never allowed
cases.actual: REJECTED (policy_invalid: cel_nesting and cel_cost at lint); at run time the rule stops at its limit and the action is denied, never allowed

cases.title: Deed chain fork: a second deed after the same parent, and an exported chain with a spliced branch
cases.expected: DETECTED (the database refuses the second child through UNIQUE (org_id, prev_hash); deedglass verify reports chain_prev_hash_mismatch or chain_seq_out_of_order at seq N)
cases.actual: DETECTED (the database refuses the second child through UNIQUE (org_id, prev_hash); deedglass verify reports chain_prev_hash_mismatch or chain_seq_out_of_order at seq N)

cases.title: Clock-skewed signed intent (iat 10 min in the future and 10 min in the past)
cases.expected: REJECTED (intent_invalid: clock window)
cases.actual: REJECTED (intent_invalid: clock window)

cases.expected: DETECTED (replies that break the phrasing rules are thrown away and the template stands; a reply that passes is marked as AI wording); the payload carries placeholders, never the org's names; the policy diff is never sent or changed
cases.actual: DETECTED (replies that break the phrasing rules are thrown away and the template stands; a reply that passes is marked as AI wording); the payload carries placeholders, never the org's names; the policy diff is never sent or changed

cases.title: Oversized and deeply nested JSON on POST /v1/actions (1 MiB + 1, args 129 deep, a body 10,000 deep)
cases.expected: REJECTED (request_too_large for 1 MiB + 1; validation_failed for args 129 deep and the 10,000-deep body) in < 200 ms; server memory grows < 64 MiB
cases.actual: REJECTED (request_too_large for 1 MiB + 1; validation_failed for args 129 deep and the 10,000-deep body) in < 200 ms; server memory grows < 64 MiB

cases.title: Log injection: tool names and args carrying ANSI escapes and newlines reach CLI output, logs and the Console
cases.expected: REDACTED (control characters escaped in every sink; 0 raw ESC bytes)
cases.actual: REDACTED (control characters escaped in every sink; 0 raw ESC bytes)

not_covered: How often models fall for injections. These cases start after the model was fooled.
A compromised Deedglass host, database superuser or seal key.

Instructions in tool descriptions are found by a heuristic (phrases, hidden Unicode, instruction tags), not by understanding intent; a reworded instruction can pass (Q01). Poisoned tool results and slow-drip responses are not scanned.
Denial of service at scale. J04 checks one agent's budget, not a flood.
The supply chain beyond `govulncheck` (S35 adds the SBOM and container scanning).
The V0 cases marked retired: each names the V7 test that checks the control instead.
What L2 can't see: effects outside Postgres, writes to tables outside the publication, and proxy-mode SQL servers (no marker to bind). `docs/WITNESS.md` lists them.

Production network rules for private ranges: the suite runs in dev with the private-network override so it can reach its own loopback servers. Metadata, link-local and cross-host targets stay blocked even then (K01, K02); the prod-only rules are covered by the egress corpus (`internal/connector/egress`).
